definition: d = min |e| s.t. De=0, Ge=1 (unit weights)
scope: circuit distance of THIS r=3 DEM under this noise family; not the code distance, not asymptotic

upper_bound.note: the witness is checkable by inspection: it fires no detector and flips the observable

flat_lower_bound.method: root-only branch-dual tree = the flat exact dual, checked bound-only; no branching, no solver
flat_lower_bound.interpretation: the LP relaxation of the distance problem is essentially vacuous (bound 1.0 against an upper bound of 12): unlike per-shot decoding, where the flat dual closes 99.15% of instances, the distance instance's relaxation is far from tight

honest_note: the branch-dual ladder did NOT close the tight lower bound (T=11) within a 200k-node budget: certifying a distance lower bound is exactly the regime where branch-and-bound is expected to be expensive, and the paper says so rather than hiding the budget
verdict: UPPER 12 (witness exhibited and hand-verified); no nontrivial certified LOWER bound achieved -- a measured limit of the method, reported as such

observable_scope.consequence: the shipped memory-Z circuit declares ONE OBSERVABLE_INCLUDE, so this DEM can only bound the SELECTED-observable fault weight; bounding d_DEM over all 12 logicals requires a circuit declaring all 12 observables -- named as future work, not claimed

renamed: d_DEM (selected-observable fault weight under the declared DEM) -- NOT the full circuit distance, which minimizes over every logical-action row and would need a circuit declaring all 12 observables
